title: TokenScale: Timely and Accurate Autoscaling for Disaggregated LLM Serving with Token Velocity
technique: autoscaling for PD-disaggregated serving using Token Velocity (max tokens/s per stage) as leading indicator, plus Convertible Decoders that run prefill during bursts

optimized_metrics.evidence: the scaling policy must be adaptive, applying rapid scaling for prefillers to meet TTFT SLOs while precisely managing decoders to sustain TPOT SLOs
To avoid overprovisioning, we need to define the requirements for cost-efficient dynamic resource scaling for both prefiller and decoder instances
leading to significant Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and Time-Per-Output-Token (TPOT) SLO violations and costly over-provisioning
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: assign different TTFT targets based on input length: 250 ms for short requests (< 256 tokens), 400 ms for medium requests (< 1024 tokens)

optimized_metrics.evidence: The TPOT SLO is fixed at 100 ms across all cases
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: The TPOT SLO is fixed at 100 ms across all cases

headline_claim.text: TokenScale improves SLO attainment from 50-88% to 80-96% and reduces costs by 4-14% over state-of-the-art systems, including DistServe, BlitzScale, and AIBrix

metric_definitions.definition_quote: This metric represents the maximum number of tokens that the instance can release in a second with the current allocated resource, for identifying the resource bottleneck of the system.
metric_definitions.notes: per stage: Prefill Velocity V_P (max input-token processing rate), Network Velocity V_N (max KV transfer rate), Decode Velocity V_D

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Decode Velocity (VD) is the maximum rate at which decoders drain tokens, measured as the number of tokens completed per unit time. It differs from generation throughput: from a memory perspective, generation throughput measures how quickly GPU memory is allocated during token generation, whereas Decode Velocity reflects how quickly memory is released as tokens are finalized.
metric_definitions.notes: capacity metric (memory-release rate), not an achieved throughput

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We follow the SLO standards defined in prior works [35], which assign different TTFT targets based on input length: 250 ms for short requests (< 256 tokens), 400 ms for medium requests (< 1024 tokens), and 2000 ms for long requests (up to 8192 tokens). The TPOT SLO is fixed at 100 ms across all cases.
metric_definitions.notes: length-bucketed TTFT SLO; TTFT/TPOT/SLO attainment themselves not formally defined; overall attainment appears to be requests meeting both TTFT and TPOT (ablation reports TTFT and TPOT attainment separately and an overall rate)

slo_spec: TTFT 250/400/2000 ms by prompt length (<256/<1024/<=8192 tokens), TPOT 100 ms; taken from Azure-trace prior work [35] and said to be widely adopted incl. MLPerf.
load_regime: trace replay (Azure Code/Conversation, BurstGPT) scaled to ~22 RPS average
tradeoff_acknowledged: Cost vs attainment: lower output-length predictor accuracy raises GPUs from 7.5 to 8.9 (and ~2% lower attainment); no named metric degraded by the method
workloads: Azure Code, Azure Conversation, BurstGPT traces
extractor_notes: Core contribution is a new capacity metric (Token Velocity) used as the scaling signal, not a latency metric. Cost is measured as number of GPUs (not $). SLO attainment aggregation (mean over requests meeting both SLOs) not explicitly defined in text read. Baselines: DistServe, BlitzScale, AIBrix.
load_class_quote: A custom load generator replays the traces, reproducing their input/output token distributions and request arrival patterns (§VI-A, Azure Conversation/Code, BurstGPT)
repass_log: SLO_ATT and COST: abstract result quotes replaced by design statements (§I requirement 'meet TTFT SLOs ... sustain TPOT SLOs'; §II 'cost-efficient dynamic resource scaling')
TTFT/TPOT constraints: design; stat_basis explicit (threshold attainment)
